g.text: placer physics · the Boise Basin · the whole of human history in one cube

svg.text: shake: heavies sink through the light stuff. gold falls 7× faster than sand.
where the creek leaves it — a bend, from above
slow water, inside bend — gold drops out
the pan, stage by stage — shake, tilt, wash, keep
a snuffer bottle takes home the tail — black sand first, then the flakes
fool’s gold or the real thing?
poke it with a pin: gold dents, pyrite snaps
all the gold, ever — one cube
a cube ~22 m on a side — fits on one city block
two-thirds of it dug up since 1950 · ~45% is jewelry
Idaho’s chapter, not far from home:
1848 — Marshall’s flakes at Sutter’s Mill, California
Aug 1862 — Grimes & Splawn strike placers on Grimes Creek
1863–64 — Idaho City: ~6,000 people, the Northwest’s largest town
